entities.name: CFTR
observations: CFTR encodes an epithelial chloride channel; the p.Phe508del (ΔF508) mutation causes misfolding and retention in the endoplasmic reticulum, reducing functional CFTR at the apical membrane.
CFTR dysfunction in airway epithelium is associated with increased epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) activity and excessive sodium absorption.

source_tools.relevance: Search-agent investigation of CFTR ΔF508 trafficking and epithelial ion-channel physiology.

entities.name: CFTR p.Phe508del
observations: The ΔF508 deletion causes improper CFTR folding and endoplasmic-reticulum retention, producing cystic fibrosis.

entities.name: SCNN1A
observations: SCNN1A encodes the alpha subunit of ENaC, the epithelial sodium channel; ENaC activity is elevated in cystic-fibrosis airway epithelium when CFTR function is defective.

entities.name: Cystic fibrosis
observations: CFTR p.Phe508del is the common ΔF508 cystic-fibrosis mutation; defective CFTR causes abnormal epithelial ion transport, including increased airway sodium absorption.
